sections.heading: 1. Pillows by position
lines: ① Side: knees bent, pillow between your knees.
② Back: 1–2 pillows under your knees.
③ Keep your head pillow fairly thin.
④ Getting up: roll to your side, push up.

sections.heading: 2. Get prompt medical help if…
lines: Night pain doesn't ease in any position, fever,
groin numbness or bladder or bowel changes.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Koko heard she should sleep dead straight. She grits her teeth, and it feels worse.

There isn't one correct sleeping position. Comfort is the guide, and shifting around overnight is normal and helpful. On your side, bend your knees a little and put a pillow between them so the top leg doesn't twist your back. On your back, try a pillow or two under your knees.

Getting up is often the sorest bit: bend your knees, roll to your side, swing your legs over and push up with your arms.

Night pain that doesn't ease with any position, fever, groin numbness or bladder or bowel changes need prompt medical attention. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
